items.prompt: Explain why clear terms and safety protection address Omi’s stated employee risks. Fictional Omi Works gives staff inconsistent explanations of pay terms and has an unguarded machine. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Employee protection concerns the relationship between workers and their employer. Workers can face unequal bargaining power, unsafe conditions, unclear terms, income risks or unfair treatment. Government can set or support standards for working conditions, social security, contracts, health and safety, redundancy, minimum wages and fair labour practices. Explain the mechanism and affected party: a safety condition protects people doing work, while a product-quality rule protects buyers in a different relationship. Protection can improve wellbeing and trust and reduce avoidable disruption, while implementation creates administrative and resource costs. These are general principles; no current legal rate, entitlement or procedure is assumed. Clear documented terms address uncertainty, while appropriate safety controls address the separate work hazard. A product discount to customers would not solve either employee problem.

items.prompt: Explain the protected parties: fictional Omi Tools needs a machine guard for workers and accurate product information for customers. [6]

items.prompt: Explain how suitable shift and rest arrangements can protect workers. A hypothetical workshop provides inadequate breaks during a demanding shift. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Working conditions include the environment and arrangements under which people work, such as reasonable scheduling, rest, facilities and treatment. Standards can protect wellbeing and reduce exploitation, but must be communicated and followed. A firm may need to adjust staffing or facilities and bear implementation cost. Evaluate effects on workers and operation rather than assume shorter hours automatically reduce or increase productivity. A suitable rest arrangement can reduce fatigue and improve the work experience, while scheduling must keep essential tasks covered. Simply changing the product label does not protect the employee.

items.prompt: Explain how a stated social-security benefit differs from continuing-job confidence. Assume a hypothetical scheme provides a qualifying worker with stated income support during covered absence. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Social security provides protection or benefits against specified income risks under the relevant scheme, potentially including illness, maternity or later-life needs depending on its terms. It is not the same as job security, confidence that a job continues. Contributions and eligibility determine how a scheme operates; do not invent benefit amounts or assume every risk is covered. Protection can support households when earnings are interrupted and can involve costs for contributors. The benefit addresses the income interruption, not a guarantee that the job lasts forever. Its usefulness depends on coverage and access under the scheme.

items.prompt: Explain why clearly recorded terms can reduce Eha’s pay and hours confusion. Fictional Eha Repairs gives different verbal accounts of a clerk’s normal hours and pay. [6]
items.canonical_answer: An employment contract records the agreement between employer and employee, including relevant work, pay, hours and responsibilities. Clear terms can reduce uncertainty and give a reference when differences arise. Documentation alone does not ensure fairness or compliance, and a written clause does not establish that every possible term is lawful. The concept here is clarity of the employment relationship rather than detailed legal drafting. A clear agreed record helps both parties understand expectations and identify a disagreement. The employer still needs to honour appropriate terms; paper alone does not settle every dispute.

items.prompt: Explain how guarding and suitable instruction can address Ota’s stated hazard. Fictional Ota Goods has an exposed moving part that a suitable guard can cover. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Health-and-safety protection seeks to reduce workplace hazards through suitable equipment, safe systems, instruction and monitoring. Identify the hazard and the measure that controls it. Information helps staff use equipment correctly but may not replace a physical guard or repaired fault. Training can be on-the-job or off-the-job according to the need, and competence should be checked. Protection can benefit workers and reduce operational interruption while requiring resources. The guard addresses contact with the stated hazard, while instruction and maintenance support continued effectiveness. A general motivational bonus is not the same control.

items.prompt: Explain why a disappearing role creates a worker-protection issue distinct from misconduct. A fictional enterprise closes a production line and no longer requires a particular role. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Redundancy concerns a job no longer needed, not necessarily poor performance by its holder. Protection can aim for fair consultation, clear reasons, suitable notice or support and consideration of alternatives under applicable arrangements. The precise process and entitlements depend on the rules; this lesson does not prescribe them. A firm may need to reorganise, but that does not make the affected worker’s interests irrelevant. Explain the operational reason and assess realistic alternatives or support rather than label the worker incompetent. Protection concerns fair treatment during that change.

items.prompt: Explain how a binding hypothetical wage floor affects Hena’s workers and costs. Assume a hypothetical wage floor rises above fictional Hena Works’ covered workers’ current hourly pay. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A minimum wage is a wage floor applying under the relevant arrangement. If a worker’s covered pay is below a binding enforced floor, raising it improves that worker’s pay and can increase the employer’s wage bill. Effects depend on the level, coverage, enforcement and responses such as prices, staffing, productivity or margins. Do not invent a current rate or claim a floor automatically raises pay for every worker. Those already above it may have no direct mandated increase. The firm must plan for the stated higher pay requirement if it applies and is enforced. Workers gain earnings, while the business needs to assess costs and feasible adjustments rather than assume one inevitable response.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: A minimum wage is a wage floor applying under the relevant arrangement.

items.prompt: Explain why credible reporting and review matter when Nara’s worker raises a concern. Fictional Nara Stores penalises a worker for raising a genuine safety concern instead of investigating it. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Protection against unfair labour practices seeks fair treatment in employment decisions and relationships, including concerns about discrimination, victimisation or improper conduct under the relevant rules. A credible response needs clear standards, access to raise concerns and fair assessment of evidence. Disagreement with a decision is not by itself proof of an unlawful practice; identify conduct and assess the case. These general concepts do not decide an individual legal complaint. A fair reporting and review route can address retaliation risk and encourage hazards to be reported. A slogan about teamwork without changing the response would offer weaker protection.

items.prompt: Evaluate education alone against a combined non-discrimination and confidential-support approach at Tula. At fictional Tula Print, a capable worker is excluded from ordinary opportunities because colleagues speculate about HIV status. Management considers an education session alone or a fair-treatment policy with confidential reporting and action. [8]
items.canonical_answer: Government can support non-discrimination, confidential handling of relevant personal information, accurate workplace education and access to prevention, care and support. Protection should respond to actual capability and workplace needs rather than assumptions about perceived HIV status. The [ILO workplace principles](https://www.ilo.org/publications/ilo-code-practice-hivaids-and-world-work) emphasise non-discrimination, confidentiality and care. A policy needs accessible complaints and implementation, not simply a statement on a wall. Education can challenge stigma but may not by itself stop unfair decisions; oversight and fair processes also matter. This explains general protection approaches and does not prescribe medical treatment or determine an individual legal claim. Education can correct misinformation, but the stated exclusion also needs a response to conduct and decisions. Prefer education combined with enforceable workplace standards, confidential reporting and fair access to opportunities. Avoid requiring public disclosure as a condition of respect; assess the job and actual needs instead of rumours.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Government can support non-discrimination, confidential handling of relevant personal information, accurate workplace education and access to prevention, care and support.

items.prompt: Evaluate whether guarding and monitoring address Nela’s risk better than information alone. A hypothetical safety standard requires fictional Nela Goods to guard an exposed machine. A suitable effective guard is available and the cost is manageable. [8]
items.canonical_answer: A protection measure should address a specified risk and be practical to implement. Compare its worker benefits, employer adjustments, public resources and possible unintended effects. A minimum-pay rule can improve earnings for covered workers paid below it, while increasing their employer’s wage cost if it applies and is enforced. A safety condition can prevent avoidable harm and disruption but needs equipment, instruction and checking. Cost alone does not show a measure should be abandoned; identify whether a proportionate implementation can preserve protection. Do not assume a rule guarantees compliance or that every employer responds by cutting jobs. The guard directly addresses the stated hazard, while instruction and checks help it work. Prefer implementation with monitoring to ignoring the risk. A leaflet alone would not physically guard the machine, even if it improves awareness.

items.prompt:
Fictional Hela Works has unclear employment terms and a worker excluded from ordinary opportunities on rumours about HIV status despite being capable. It compares a general information poster with a combined approach: clear terms, non-discrimination standards, confidential reporting and fair follow-up. No legal rate or medical treatment is specified.

a(i) State two employee-protection measures. [2]
a(ii) State two matters to consider when judging a protection measure’s effectiveness. [2]
b State two purposes of clear employment terms. [2]
c Explain how a combined approach can protect Hela’s affected worker. [6]
d Evaluate it against a general poster alone. [8]
items.canonical_answer: a(i) Clear employment contracts and safe-work standards. a(ii) Whether it addresses the risk and whether it is implemented. b Clarifying pay and clarifying work responsibilities or hours. c Education can challenge misinformation; fair-treatment standards guide opportunity decisions; confidential reporting can reveal exclusion and allow fair follow-up without public speculation. The response should assess capability rather than perceived status. d A poster is inexpensive and can supply information but does not itself resolve unclear terms or exclusion. Prefer the combined approach with responsible follow-up and review, despite its administrative cost, because it addresses the actual conduct and relationship. A policy that nobody implements would not secure the intended protection.

items.prompt:
Fictional Omi Print has documented employment terms, but a capable worker faces exclusion based on perceived HIV status. A combined information, confidential-reporting and fair-response approach is available. Management compares it with education alone. For part (b) only, reliable review shows that confidential reports under the combined approach are not being investigated, so exclusion continues. Other facts remain unchanged.

b Evaluate it after the failure to investigate reports becomes known. Explain whether the judgement should change. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a The combination addresses misinformation and unfair conduct, with a confidential route to raise concerns. It is preferable to education alone if implemented fairly and monitored, while requiring resources and careful information handling. b Continued exclusion and ignored reports show the implementation condition has failed. Retain the protection objectives but repair accountability, investigation and follow-up, and use an appropriate independent review route where needed. Education alone is still insufficient. The judgement changes from endorsing the stated design to requiring effective implementation before claiming success; the affected worker’s capability and dignity remain central.
